name: Treasury and Dollar Statecraft
overview: The Treasury camp holds that America's deepest power is financial: the dollar, the Treasury market every central bank holds, and a Fed whose word markets trust. Spent with care, that power does what armies cannot. Sanctions and licenses squeeze Iran and open or close Venezuela and Russia; tariffs become bargaining chips on legal ground the trade court can uphold; and dollar stablecoins carry the currency into economies whose own money is failing (Bessent, Oct 27). The program is national strength through credibility: no fired Fed chair, no bond rout, managed trade instead of shock, and reindustrialization paced so that markets will fund it. Greer brings the Lighthizer school's case that China trade must be managed, built on Section 301 cases.

Its members' fortunes and careers were made in the markets this program protects. Bessent ran money for Soros and then Key Square; Warsh took $10.2M in fees from Druckenmiller's office and married into the Lauder fortune; Greer was Lighthizer's chief of staff and then a King & Spalding trade partner and lobbyist. Their standing depends on markets believing them, so calm markets are both creed and capital. Turf counts as much: sanctions, licenses and the Treasury-held Venezuelan oil account make Treasury the gate every deal faction must pass. No donor is tied to a position.

Acts depart from words in three places. Sanctions are sold as leverage, yet Treasury's licenses also carry the Deal-Capital track: a diesel license 'at President Trump's direction' (Oct 9) and the Lukoil sale-talks license extended to Nov 21 (Oct 21), so Treasury's own tool serves other people's deals. Fed independence is the creed, yet Warsh and Bessent pursue a new Treasury-Fed accord that pulls the two closer. And Bessent divested his soybean farmland only in the week before he helped announce a $12B farm aid package tied to the China trade fight (Dec 2025): the stake went, but on the eve of a decision it touched.

Precedent: the 1951 Treasury-Fed Accord, when Treasury let the Fed stop pegging bond yields and so created modern Fed independence. It breaks here: Warsh's 'new accord' runs the other way, toward Treasury, while the president attacks a Board whose hike his own chair voted for (my reading).

Axios reported that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent pressed Commerce to act on suspected diversion of Nvidia chips to China. Commerce disputed the reported confrontation. A restriction takes effect only after the administration acts to impose it.

paras: Position.
Apr 2025: talked Trump out of firing Powell. Sep 16: a 12-0 hike under Warsh. Oct 28: held 10-2, with Cook and Hammack wanting a hike.
Why the faction does it. A fired chair or a politicized Board would raise the cost of the debt Treasury must sell and spook the bond market its members come from (documented fit; no donor tied).
Who and why.
Bessent. Posture: guardian of Fed credibility. Interest: Treasury sells the debt, so yields are his scorecard, and the planned accord keeps Treasury in the room on the balance sheet.

Warsh. Posture: independent inflation-fighter. Interest: his market standing is the asset, and a cut on Trump's order would spend it. He sold over $100M of assets before May 22 to undisclosed buyers; no link to a decision is shown. Tillis's threat shaped how loudly he could side with Trump.
Say versus do. Independence is the slogan; an accord that ties the Fed's balance sheet to Treasury's needs is the program (my reading).

Stance audit. Treasury favored market credibility and sought a closer accord. The FOMC voted on rates. The September and October votes are committee actions. Assess advocacy over the Fed chair and the accord separately. Borrowing costs and institutional influence are Treasury stakes. The ledger records professional financial ties and identifies no issue-specific donor. Preserve both the credibility and influence objectives. A rate result alone gives no evidence of a Treasury stance reversal.

Why the faction does it. Sanctions are Treasury's own war: they keep Iran policy in its hands during the strike hold and cost less in oil prices than bombing (my reading).
Who and why.

Bessent. Posture: 'absolute isolation'. Interest: turf and markets. The squeeze makes Treasury central while the Pentagon waits, and Brent near $113 (Oct 27) is the price shock his program exists to avoid.
Say versus do. The designations are acts, but each round ships with wind-down licenses (EE, FF-1, GG, HH) that soften it.
